title: Runtime Safety Assistant: Batch & Cache Strategy Flow
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Design an interactive Runtime Safety Assistant in the Redwood Console that guides engineers through safe batching and caching configuration. The assistant should surface concrete trade-offs (latency, cost, failure modes), suggest conservative and aggressive profiles, allow quick simulation of edge cases, and wire up explainable toggles for automatic fallbacks. This ticket drives a high-fidelity prototype, acceptance criteria, and handoff artifacts for engineering.

Why this now: teams are hesitant to adopt aggressive batching/kv-cache settings because they lack visibility into edge-case regressions and fallback behavior. A step-by-step assistant reduces cognitive load, improves adoption of cost-saving settings, and lowers risk of production regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype shows 3-step flow: Analyze workload -> Suggest profiles -> Simulate & Apply
Each suggested profile includes estimated latency uplift, token-cost delta, and regression-risk explanation
Simulation playground can run 3 canned scenarios (cold-start, burst, long-context) with predicted outcomes
UI exposes an explainable toggle for each automation (auto-batching, prefix-caching, KV-merge) with linked docs
Design annotations include ARIA accessibility notes and mobile/embedded console variants
Engineer sign-off: feasibility notes captured and handoff checklist created
notes: Focus on making recommendations reversible and clearly labeled with units (ms / $ / regression probability). Avoid adding new knobs that cannot be audited — every automatic change must produce an audit log entry. Consider tying a telemetry event to the 'simulate' button to collect anonymized outcomes for improving future recommendations.
